answer: A new agent must stake a bond that vests slowly: to forge an identity it first locks funds for weeks, and each extra identity multiplies that lockup, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand bonds. Reputation then accrues only through attested work, and peers weight endorsements by stake age, so a fresh swarm starts at the bottom of every ridge of trust. By dawn of each epoch, cheap identities have earned nothing while honest agents keep their vested standing, so mass fakery pays upfront and gains slowly.
